disclaimer: Researched via web search (not invented), each cross-referenced against at least one source noted per entry. Coordinates are best-effort - exact for named landmarks with published locations, area-center estimates where noted in the 'source' field. Worth a spot-check before the site is shown to anyone, but this is real content, not placeholder scaffolding.

places.name: Trachones Stream Path
places.description: One of only two streams in the Athens basin with a natural, unculverted mouth; it gathers water off Hymettus through Argyroupoli, Ilioupoli and Elliniko before reaching the sea at Alimos, with surviving reed banks and bird life known mainly to local ramblers.
places.source: Local nature blogs heliosperiigisis.blogspot.com and geomythiki.blogspot.com, plus notia.gr reporting on 'Ρέμα Τραχώνων'.

places.name: Ymittos Grove, Argyroupoli
places.description: A small municipal grove on Kiafas street in Argyroupoli itself, with shaded paths, calisthenics gear and picnic spots - a five-minute local walk, not a destination park.
places.source: Moovit transit listing and municipal directories for Άλσος Υμηττού, Kiafas 35, Argyroupoli.

places.name: Pikrodafni Stream Path
places.description: The last stream in southern Attica that still runs in a natural bed for part of its course, flowing off western Hymettus to the sea between Palaio Faliro and Kalamaki; volunteer groups run clean-up walks along it.
places.source: Greek Wikipedia 'Ρέμα της Πικροδάφνης'; Athens Voice and Agios Dimitrios Notia News features on the stream.

places.name: Agios Dimitrios Municipal Vegetable Gardens
places.description: 45 allotment plots on a once-derelict municipal lot at Ethnomartyron 61, where local families grow organic vegetables and donate a share to the municipality's social pantry.
places.source: Δήμος Αγίου Δημητρίου official site (dad.gr) and Athens Voice feature on the gardens.

places.name: Cave of the Nymphs (Vari Cave)
places.description: A rock-cut cave on the southern slope of Hymettus above Vari, carved with reliefs by the sculptor Archedemos in the 5th century BC as a sanctuary to Pan and the Nymphs; unmarked and rarely visited today.
places.source: Greek Wikipedia 'Σπήλαιο Νυμφολήπτου' (coordinates 37°51'30"N 23°48'06"E).

places.name: Profitis Ilias Chapel above Ano Glyfada
places.description: A tiny hilltop chapel on the southern flank of Hymettus at about 400m elevation, reached by a short path above Ano Glyfada, with a view over the southern suburbs, Piraeus and, on clear days, the Acropolis.
places.source: noupou.gr 'Το μικρό εκκλησάκι του Προφήτη Ηλία πάνω από τη Γλυφάδα' and mthymettosgreece.com trail notes.

places.name: Monastery of Agios Ioannis Prodromos, Kareas
places.description: An 11th-12th century Byzantine monastery tucked into a pine forest on the western slope of Hymettus above Vyronas, next to the ancient 'Kara' quarries, with a path continuing south along the mountainside.
places.source: monastiria.gr entry and Vice Greece feature 'Καρέας: Ένα Κομμάτι Πόλης που Πήρε τα Βουνά'.

places.name: Agia Sofia Chapel, Chroma (Vari)
places.description: A small neighbourhood chapel in the quiet Chroma district of Vari, built as a long-standing wish of local residents rather than for pilgrimage - a stop on a walk through the area's semi-rural streets.
places.source: Municipality of Vari-Voula-Vouliagmeni church listings referencing the Chroma neighbourhood chapel of Agia Sofia and her daughters.

places.name: Tourkovounia Abandoned Quarries
places.description: Disused stone quarries worked 1937-1976 by the Kekrops company, scarring the hills above Galatsi and Kypseli, now crossed by informal trails with views from the Acropolis to the Saronic Gulf.
places.source: Rib and Sea travel blog photo walk, D-EuZin hiking club trip reports, Greek Wikipedia 'Τουρκοβούνια'.

places.name: Attiko Alsos (Attica Grove)
places.description: A hillside grove wedged between Kypseli, Nea Filothei and Galatsi, adjoining the Tourkovounia quarries - a plain neighbourhood green lung rather than a showcase park.
places.source: utopiazone.gr walk report 'Μια σαββατιάτικη βόλτα στα υποτιμημένα Τουρκοβούνια και στο Αττικό Άλσος'.

places.name: Strefi Hill
places.description: A scruffy, much-loved neighbourhood hill above Exarcheia and Neapoli with dirt paths, a small football pitch and a view over the rooftops to the Acropolis - a local hangout, not a sight to tick off.
places.source: inexarchia.gr profile of the hill and Athens Voice 'Λόφος Στρέφη: Η μεταμόρφωση'.

places.name: Antonis Tritsis Park
places.description: A former quarry and municipal nursery in Ilion turned into Attica's largest park, with four artificial lakes hosting over 140 bird species - used by locals for weekend walks and cycling, not by tour groups.
places.source: Greek Wikipedia 'Μητροπολιτικό Πάρκο Αντώνης Τρίτσης' and parkotritsis.gr.

places.name: Mount Aigaleo Ridge
places.description: A low, largely overlooked ridge separating western Athens from the Thriasio plain, with quiet paths and a view over Piraeus and the Saronic Gulf that almost nobody outside the western suburbs bothers with.
places.source: travelvibe.eu feature 'Όρος Αιγάλεω: Περπατώντας στον Άγνωστο φυσικό παράδεισο της Δυτικής Αθήνας'.

places.name: Koutouki Cave
places.description: The only show cave in Attica, found by accident in 1926 on the eastern slopes of Hymettus above Paiania - a single large chamber divided by limestone curtains, usually quiet outside weekends.
places.source: exploringgreece.tv 'Το άγνωστο και μοναδικό επισκέψιμο σπήλαιο στην Αττική'.

places.name: Davelis Cave
places.description: A quarried cave on Penteli mountain, once a sanctuary of Pan and later a Byzantine hermitage, riddled with unfinished 1970s military tunnels - a favourite of local urban explorers and legend-tellers, not tour buses.
places.source: Greek Wikipedia 'Σπήλαιο Πεντέλης', apotis4stis5.com, penteli.gov.gr municipal history page.

places.name: Aloula Marble Quarry
places.description: A worked-out Pentelic marble quarry near Dionysos that locals treat as an informal open-air museum of stone-cutting relics, with tool marks and abandoned marble blocks still in place.
places.source: mixanitouxronou.gr 'Αλούλα. Το εγκαταλελειμμένο λατομείο της Πεντέλης' and oryktosploutos.net photo essay.

places.name: Dionysos Marble Quarry
places.description: An abandoned marble quarry above the village of Dionysos whose stone matches ancient Pentelic marble in colour and grain; leftover cutting terraces and machinery make for an odd, quiet walk.
places.source: LiFO photo essay 'Οδοιπορικό στο εγκαταλελειμμένο λατομείο του Διονύσου'.

places.name: Old Chalandri Railway Station
places.description: The well-preserved station building of the old Athens-Lavrio steam line (nicknamed 'Thirio'), standing next to a playground by the church of Agia Anna in Chalandri, silent since the line closed in 1957.
places.source: mixanitouxronou.gr feature on the historic Athens-Lavrio railway and its surviving stations.

places.name: Forgotten Railway Station Plot, Kifisia
places.description: Remains of an early station that once linked Kifisia to Nea Erythraia and Dionysos sit fenced inside an ordinary residential plot - a forerunner of the famous 'Thirio' train that most passersby never notice.
places.source: mixanitouxronou.gr 'Ένας ξεχασμένος σιδηροδρομικός σταθμός μέσα σε οικόπεδο στην Κηφισιά'. Coordinates are an area estimate - no exact address published.

places.name: Vravrona Wetland (Erasinos River Mouth)
places.description: A protected marshland at the mouth of the Erasinos river next to the ancient sanctuary of Artemis, with reed beds and wading birds; locals walk it far more than the adjoining archaeological site.
places.source: zougla.gr 'Βόλτα στον υγρότοπο της Βραυρώνας - Ποταμός Ερασίνος' and topoguide.gr Natura 2000 wetlands page.

places.name: Artemida Wetland (Alyki Loutsas)
places.description: A 500-acre former salt marsh behind Agios Nikolaos beach in Artemida, ringed by reeds and tamarisk, hosting around 170 recorded bird species - protected on paper since 2018 but visited mostly by dog-walkers and birders.
places.source: Hellenic Ornithological Society 'Υγρότοπος Αρτέμιδας: όαση για την άγρια ζωή' and Greek Wikipedia 'Υγρότοπος Αρτέμιδος Αττικής'.

places.name: Rapentosa Waterfall
places.description: A small waterfall on the Rapentosa stream, which starts in an old marble quarry on Penteli's northern slope and passes under the Dionysos-Nea Makri road before reaching a modest dam - a minor, little-signposted spot.
places.source: exploringgreece.tv 'Μονοήμερη εκδρομή: Ο καταρράκτης της Αττικής που θα σε εντυπωσιάσει'.

places.name: Rathes of Kapandriti
places.description: A forested hollow near the village of Kapandriti at the eastern foot of Parnitha, fed by small local springs (Miliatzi, Kostigialesi, Ai Giorgis) - a plane-tree shaded spot known to nearby villages, not to Athens tourism.
places.source: exploringgreece.tv 'Ράθες Καπανδριτίου: Η μυστική γωνιά δίπλα στην Αθήνα' and a matching Wikiloc trail log.

places.name: Amphiareion of Oropos
places.description: A minor sanctuary-and-spa complex in a pine valley near Oropos, dedicated to the healer-hero Amphiaraos, with a small theatre, stoa and a sacred spring still flowing from a Roman-era cistern - usually empty of visitors.
places.source: Greek Wikipedia 'Αμφιαράειο' and Δήμος Ωρωπού official site oropos.gov.gr.

places.name: Rhamnous
places.description: The fortified ruins of an ancient deme on the northeast Attic coast near Agia Marina, with the marble sanctuary of Nemesis half-standing among pines - one of the least-visited classical sites in Attica.
places.source: iefimerida.gr 'Ραμνούς: Ο αρχαίος δήμος της Αττικής που δεν άγγιξε ο χρόνος' and Greek Wikipedia 'Ραμνούντας'.

places.name: Schinias-Marathon National Park Wetland
places.description: Attica's largest wetland, backing onto the pine-fringed Schinias beach and Marathon plain, with over 240 recorded bird species - the wildlife-layer example named directly in the brief.
places.source: Greek Wikipedia 'Εθνικό Πάρκο Σχινιά Μαραθώνα' and votaniki.gr Natura 2000 profile.

places.name: Mount Parnitha National Forest
places.description: Attica's highest and most densely forested mountain, a wildlife refuge and the only place in Greece with wild red deer (Cervus elaphus) - the wildlife-layer example named directly in the brief.
places.source: mountparnitha.gr visitor pages and Athens Voice 'Τα ελάφια της Πάρνηθας'.

places.name: Oropos Wetland (Asopos Mouth)
places.description: A smaller, less-studied coastal wetland where the Asopos river meets the sea near Skala Oropou, offering reed beds and shallow lagoons well off the usual Attica nature-trip circuit.
places.source: topoguide.gr Natura 2000 wetlands listing for Attica, 'Υγρότοπος Ωρωπού'. Thin sourcing - worth double-checking.

places.name: Keratea Old Railway Station
places.description: The surviving station building of the old Lavrio narrow-gauge line, with two freight wagons still parked in front of it - a quiet relic inside an otherwise ordinary market town.
places.source: Greek Wikipedia 'Σιδηροδρομική Γραμμή Λαυρίου - Αγίων Αναργύρων' and dtert.gr (Friends of the Railway Society) station photo archive.

places.name: Daskaleio Railway Station
places.description: A small restored station on the same disused Lavrio line near Keratea, where seven old carriages were being converted into an eco-tourism stop - an obscure stub of the network most drivers speed straight past.
places.source: money-tourism.gr and vrisko.gr address listing for Δασκαλειό, Κερατέα. Thinner sourcing - worth double-checking.
